candidate_sentence_map.S1: Gigasun continued to expand during 2025, with stronger production and operating profitability, although the Group remained loss-making after financial items and faced a weaker financial position.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Total revenue increased 9.8% to SEK 239.7 million from SEK 218.3 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Net revenue from electricity sales rose 9.9% to SEK 203.2 million and represented 85% of total revenue, while other operating income, mainly subsidies, increased to SEK 36.5 million from SEK 33.5 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Revenue growth was supported by higher production but constrained by lower average prices, a larger share of electricity sold to the grid, revised tariffs and adverse currency effects, which reduced revenue by SEK 18.0 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Operating expenses increased 5.5% to SEK 166.2 million, primarily reflecting the larger installed base, higher depreciation and increased maintenance costs.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Gross profit rose to SEK 195.8 million, with the gross margin unchanged at 82%.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: EBITDA increased 12.3% to SEK 163.7 million and the EBITDA margin improved to 68% from 67%.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: EBIT increased 21.1% to SEK 73.5 million, raising the operating margin to 31% from 28%.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Lower financing costs contributed to the improvement: interest expenses and similar charges declined to SEK 82.0 million from SEK 88.7 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Nevertheless, the Group reported a loss after tax of SEK 7.2 million, compared with a loss of SEK 32.9 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: The result included a negative currency effect of SEK 3.8 million and a one-off cost of SEK 3.5 million; the CEO stated that profit adjusted for these items was SEK 0.1 million, compared with negative SEK 34.7 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Operationally, produced electricity increased 30% to 327.8 million kWh, and installed capacity grew 16% to 395.8 MW from 340.1 MW through the addition of 55.7 MW.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: The portfolio comprised 216 installations at year-end.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: The company signed 17 contracts representing approximately 41.8 MW of capacity, although signed orders at year-end were reported at 16.4 MW.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: Electricity tariffs in Jiangsu and Anhui reduced realized prices per kWh by approximately 8% in the second half, with an estimated 3–4% impact on revenue from the existing portfolio.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Gigasun stated that lower financing and construction costs were expected to offset this pressure.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Refinancing agreements totaling approximately SEK 1.242 billion at 3.60% over ten years were initiated, while the SOLT4 bond was extended to 8 November 2026.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: Interest-bearing debt declined to SEK 1.383 billion from SEK 1.483 billion, but cash fell to SEK 45.1 million from SEK 89.9 million and the equity ratio decreased to 21% from 23%.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: The Group’s cash flow was negative SEK 34.9 million, as operating cash flow of SEK 101.1 million did not cover investments of SEK 208.1 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: Management stated that failure to secure further financing in 2026 would create significant uncertainty regarding the Group’s ability to continue under its current business plan.

evaluation.label: Generally yes

issues.description: The summary repeats the theme of financing challenges in S17 and S21 without adding new information, creating minor redundancy.

evaluation.justification: The summary is generally coherent with a logical flow from revenue and production growth to profitability metrics, financing, and cash flow concerns. Explanations for revenue growth and constraints are consistent (S2-S4), and operating metrics (S5-S8) logically lead to the final loss after tax (S10). The financing discussion (S17-S21) is thematically linked but contains minor repetition. No self-contradictions or severe organizational issues are present. The arithmetic relationships between segment figures and totals are not claimed to be exhaustive additive components, so differences do not constitute contradictions.
